title: Teaching social skills to autistic teens (SOP1)

sentences.en: Hello, I'm Audrey Hamilton.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是奥黛丽·汉密尔顿。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, a podcast from the American
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是来自美国

sentences.en: Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 心理学会的播客。

sentences.en: The anxiety of a new school year can affect almost any student.
sentences.zh: 新学年的焦虑几乎会影响到每一位学生。

sentences.en: They may be worried about which teachers they'll have or the prospect of meeting new classmates.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会担心自己会被分到哪个老师的班级，或者担心结识新同学的前景。

sentences.en: For students with autism spectrum disorder, meeting new people and making friends is especially challenging.
sentences.zh: 对于患有自闭症谱系障碍的学生来说，结识新朋友和交友尤其具有挑战性。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll hear from Dr. Elizabeth Logason, a psychologist who runs the program for the education and enrichment of relational skills, or peers, at UCLA, where
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将采访加州大学洛杉矶分校（UCLA）“人际关系技能教育与充实项目”（简称PEERS）的负责人、心理学家伊丽莎白·洛加森博士，该项目

sentences.en: the latest autism behavioral research is used to help teens make and keep friends.
sentences.zh: 利用最新的自闭症行为研究来帮助青少年结交并维系朋友。

sentences.en: Elizabeth Logason is a licensed clinical psychologist and assistant clinical professor of psychiatry and biobehavioral sciences at UCLA.
sentences.zh: 伊丽莎白·洛加森是一位持证临床心理学家，也是加州大学洛杉矶分校精神病学和生物行为科学系的临床助理教授。

sentences.en: She is the founder and director of the UCLA Peers Clinic, where she works directly with teens and young adults with autism spectrum disorder.
sentences.zh: 她是加州大学洛杉矶分校PEERS诊所的创始人和主任，在那里她直接为患有自闭症谱系障碍的青少年和年轻人提供服务。

sentences.en: Her research, investigating social skills training for youth from preschool to early adulthood, has been widely published and recognized.
sentences.zh: 她对从学龄前到成年早期青少年的社交技能训练进行了研究，其成果已被广泛发表并获得认可。

sentences.en: Her studies have been funded by the National Institutes of Health and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
sentences.zh: 她的研究得到了美国国立卫生研究院和疾病控制与预防中心的资助。

sentences.en: Welcome, Dr. Logason.
sentences.zh: 欢迎您，洛加森博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我参加节目。

sentences.en: The program you lead at UCLA, the Peers Program, focuses on improving social skills among high-functioning adolescents with autism using evidence-based training.
sentences.zh: 您在加州大学洛杉矶分校领导的PEERS项目，专注于利用循证训练来提高高功能自闭症青少年的社交技能。

sentences.en: Can you give us some real-life examples of how this program works?
sentences.zh: 您能给我们举一些现实生活中的例子，说明这个项目是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Sure, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然，没问题。

sentences.en: You know, one of the things that we really focus on in peers is not just social skills, which is rather broad, but really making and keeping friends.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在PEERS中真正关注的不仅仅是社交技能——这个概念太宽泛了——而是真正地去结交并维系朋友。

sentences.en: We know that having a few close friends in adolescence and adulthood is really critical to later adjustment in life.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，在青春期和成年期拥有几个亲密朋友对于日后的人生适应至关重要。

sentences.en: And so the types of skills that we focus on are things like conversational skills,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们关注的技能类型包括对话技巧，

sentences.en: knowing how to go up to a group of people and join their conversation, how to assess whether or not
sentences.zh: 知道如何走向一群人并加入他们的谈话，如何判断自己是否

sentences.en: you're accepted into those conversations, and if you're not, how to exit the conversations.
sentences.zh: 被对方接纳，如果没被接纳，又该如何退出谈话。

sentences.en: We also talk about things like having get-togethers and developing closer, more meaningful friendships with people,
sentences.zh: 我们还讨论如何组织聚会，如何与他人建立更亲密、更有意义的友谊，

sentences.en: as well as handling things like peer rejection and peer conflict.
sentences.zh: 以及如何处理同伴拒绝和同伴冲突等问题。

sentences.en: Why do autistic children need social skills training specifically, and when have you seen them gain from it?
sentences.zh: 为什么自闭症儿童特别需要社交技能训练？您在什么时候看到他们从中受益？

sentences.en: Well, you know, social skill deficits are one of the hallmark features in autism across the spectrum.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，社交技能缺陷是自闭症谱系的一个标志性特征。

sentences.en: And the way that that sort of manifests itself is in difficulty with things like social communication, knowing how to have a conversation with someone.
sentences.zh: 这种缺陷的表现形式是社交沟通困难，比如不知道如何与人交谈。

sentences.en: Also social awareness, so really understanding the social landscape in which you live, kind of picking up on social cues.
sentences.zh: 还有社交意识，即真正理解你所处的社交环境，能够捕捉到社交暗示。

sentences.en: We know that our kids really struggle with social, you know, motivation, wanting to actually engage their peers, as well as
sentences.zh: 我们知道，我们的孩子在社交动力方面确实很挣扎，比如是否真的想与同伴互动，以及

sentences.en: social cognition, which is another one of those hallmark features of autism.
sentences.zh: 社交认知，这也是自闭症的标志性特征之一。

sentences.en: And that's basically difficulty kind of putting yourself in someone else's shoes, understanding the perspectives of others.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是指难以设身处地为他人着想，难以理解他人的观点。

sentences.en: So we know that adolescents and adults with autism really struggle socially, and so of course we want to intervene and help them in this, you know, very vital and important area.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，患有自闭症的青少年和成年人在社交方面确实很吃力，因此我们当然希望进行干预，帮助他们应对这个非常关键且重要的领域。

sentences.en: Can you talk about what it is about their, this disorder that makes it so difficult for them to maintain friendships and engage with others, their, you know, others their age?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈这种障碍究竟是什么，使得他们如此难以维持友谊并与同龄人互动吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think difficulty with conversational skills, for example, makes it very, very difficult to develop meaningful and close relationships with
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为以对话技巧为例，其困难使得他们很难与人建立有意义的亲密关系，

sentences.en: people, whether they be friendships or romantic relationships, and difficulty picking up on social
sentences.zh: 无论是友谊还是浪漫关系；此外，难以捕捉社交

sentences.en: cues and understanding the perspectives of others, knowing how someone might actually react to something that we say or something that we do.
sentences.zh: 暗示和理解他人的观点，不知道别人会对我们说的话或做的事产生什么反应。

sentences.en: That sort of difficulty makes it really challenging for people with autism to develop these relationships.
sentences.zh: 这种困难使得自闭症患者建立人际关系变得非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: And you talk about engaging and even having a real conversation, but you know, these days when there's cyber bullying, there's social media, I mean,
sentences.zh: 您谈到了互动甚至进行真正的对话，但你知道，现在有网络欺凌，有社交媒体，我的意思是，

sentences.en: how is that challenging for autistic teens when it comes to, you know, making friends and interacting?
sentences.zh: 对于自闭症青少年来说，在结交朋友和互动方面，这构成了怎样的挑战？

sentences.en: You know, what's interesting about kids with autism is that they very often gravitate towards technology and computers and, and, you know, being on the internet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，自闭症孩子有趣的一点是，他们往往会被技术、电脑和上网所吸引。

sentences.en: But interestingly enough, they're not that engaged in search traditional forms of social media, like a lot of kids are on
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，他们并不像许多孩子那样热衷于传统的社交媒体形式，比如

sentences.en: Facebook, for example.
sentences.zh: 以Facebook为例。

sentences.en: But our kids in the spectrum don't tend to be involved in things like
sentences.zh: 我们谱系内的孩子往往不会参与像

sentences.en: Facebook, those types of social media.
sentences.zh: Facebook这类社交媒体。

sentences.en: They do tend to gravitate towards things like online gaming, things like World of Warcraft, and Minecraft, and things like that.
sentences.zh: 他们确实倾向于被网络游戏所吸引，比如《魔兽世界》、《我的世界》之类的游戏。

sentences.en: But there's not as much social interaction in those types of foruMs. When our kids are, though, involved with types of social media
sentences.zh: 但在这些类型的论坛中，社交互动并不多。不过，当我们的孩子参与像Facebook这样的社交媒体时，

sentences.en: like Facebook, they are more prone to actually being cyber bullied, very sadly, by their peers.
sentences.zh: 非常遗憾的是，他们更容易受到同伴的网络欺凌。

sentences.en: And so there's many different, you know, hypotheses about why that might be.
sentences.zh: 关于为什么会这样，有很多不同的假设。

sentences.en: But again, knowing that our kids aren't quite as socially savvy and aren't necessarily picking up on the same cues that the rest of us
sentences.zh: 但同样，因为知道我们的孩子社交能力没那么强，未必能捕捉到我们其他人

sentences.en: might be picking up on, they do become easier targets for bullying.
sentences.zh: 能捕捉到的那些暗示，他们确实更容易成为欺凌的目标。

sentences.en: So one of the things that we do in peers is we actually target that type of peer rejection and give them strategies for how to handle cyber bullying.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在PEERS中做的一件事，就是专门针对这种同伴拒绝，并为他们提供应对网络欺凌的策略。

sentences.en: Well, going back to the program itself, I know that it relies a lot on role playing to help students understand how to behave.
sentences.zh: 回到项目本身，我知道它很大程度上依赖角色扮演来帮助学生理解如何表现。

sentences.en: What are some examples of these social situations they face during training?
sentences.zh: 他们在训练中面临的社交情境有哪些例子？

sentences.en: Well, I'm glad you asked.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你问这个问题。

sentences.en: I love talking about the program and the skills that we teach.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢谈论这个项目以及我们教授的技能。

sentences.en: You know, we basically teach two types of skills.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们基本上教授两种类型的技能。

sentences.en: We teach sort of how to develop meaningful relationships with other people.
sentences.zh: 我们教授如何与他人建立有意义的关系。

sentences.en: And we also teach our kids how to handle things like peer rejection and peer conflict, because we know that that's very, very common, unfortunately, for a lot of our teens and
sentences.zh: 我们也教孩子们如何处理同伴拒绝和同伴冲突，因为我们知道，不幸的是，这对我们许多青少年和

sentences.en: adults.
sentences.zh: 成年人来说是非常非常普遍的。

sentences.en: So to give you an example of how we might handle sort of, you know, making new friends, meeting new people.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，说明我们如何处理结交新朋友、认识新人的问题。

sentences.en: So we mentioned that, you know, one of the things that people often have to do in order to meet new friends is to go up and join conversations with people.
sentences.zh: 我们提到过，人们为了结识新朋友通常需要做的一件事，就是走过去加入别人的谈话。

sentences.en: But what do you think that most adults might tell a teen to do in that situation?
sentences.zh: 但你认为大多数成年人会告诉青少年在这种情况下该怎么做？

sentences.en: Like imagine they're at a party, they don't really know anyone, and they want to get to know the other people.
sentences.zh: 比如想象他们在一个聚会上，谁也不认识，但想认识其他人。

sentences.en: What would an adult tell that teen to do?
sentences.zh: 成年人会告诉那个青少年怎么做？

sentences.en: Just go up, introduce yourself, find something in common.
sentences.zh: 直接走过去，自我介绍，找共同点。

sentences.en: Okay, well, they definitely tell them to go up and introduce themselves.
sentences.zh: 好的，他们确实会告诉他们走过去自我介绍。

sentences.en: I mean, we hear that time and time again from kids.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们一次又一次地从孩子们那里听到这一点。

sentences.en: They're also told up to go, they're told to go up and say hi.
sentences.zh: 他们也被告知要走过去打个招呼。

sentences.en: But if you step back and you really think about what that would look like, I mean, imagine if a teen were to walk up to another group of teens and say hi,
sentences.zh: 但如果你退后一步，仔细想想那会是什么样子，想象一下，如果一个青少年走到另一群青少年面前说“嗨”，

sentences.en: you know, and kind of wave their hand or, or even worse, say hi, you know, I'm Liz, and kind of put their hand out to shake hands.
sentences.zh: 挥挥手，或者更糟的是，说“嗨，我是莉兹”，然后伸出手想握手。

sentences.en: That's not really what kids who are socially accepted are naturally doing.
sentences.zh: 那并不是社交上受欢迎的孩子自然会做的事情。

sentences.en: It's not what we call an ecologically valid social skill, what people who are socially accepted would naturally do.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们所说的“生态效度”社交技能，即社交上受欢迎的人自然会做的事情。

sentences.en: So in peers, what we try to do is actually teach what people who are socially accepted do in these real world situations.
sentences.zh: 所以在PEERS中，我们尝试教授的是社交上受欢迎的人在这些现实世界情境中真正会做的事情。

sentences.en: So instead of going up and saying hi, or going up and introducing ourselves, instead what we would teach our kids to do is first start by just kind
sentences.zh: 所以，与其走过去说“嗨”或自我介绍，我们教给孩子的方法是先从

sentences.en: of listening and watching the conversation.
sentences.zh: 倾听和观察谈话开始。

sentences.en: And you mentioned something a moment ago, what do you think we're kind of watching and listening for?
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了这一点，你认为我们在观察和倾听什么？

sentences.en: We're listening for an in, some, some way to join the conversation that would be interesting.
sentences.zh: 我们在寻找切入点，寻找一种有趣的方式加入谈话。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you kind of mentioned about the sort of this common interest, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，你提到了共同兴趣，对吧？

sentences.en: So we're listening for the topic, first of all, and we're trying to make sure that we actually have something in common with the people that are talking, that we know something
sentences.zh: 所以我们首先是在听话题，我们要确保我们和正在交谈的人确实有共同点，我们了解这个话题，

sentences.en: about the topic, that we have something to contribute.
sentences.zh: 我们有东西可以贡献。

sentences.en: Now, while we're doing that, do you think that we should be sort of staring at the group as we're listening?
sentences.zh: 那么，在我们这样做的时候，你认为我们应该在倾听时盯着那群人看吗？

sentences.en: Seems awkward.
sentences.zh: 看起来很尴尬。

sentences.en: It would be a little bit awkward.
sentences.zh: 那会有点尴尬。

sentences.en: Yeah, we probably don't want to stare at them.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们可能不想盯着他们看。

sentences.en: So what a lot of people do is they'll actually use a prop.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人实际上会使用道具。

sentences.en: They'll have a phone or like a gaming device or something like that, but they'll be kind
sentences.zh: 他们会拿着手机或游戏设备之类的东西，看起来好像在看短信，

sentences.en: of looking at their phone, maybe appearing like they're looking at text messages or something, but really they're eavesdropping.
sentences.zh: 但实际上是在偷听。

sentences.en: We just don't want to look like we're eavesdropping.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不想看起来像是在偷听。

sentences.en: So once we've sort of listened, figured out what the topic is, and decided that we want to join this conversation, we're going to wait for something.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦我们听了一会儿，弄清楚了话题，并决定加入谈话，我们就要等待一个时机。

sentences.en: So what do you think we're waiting for?
sentences.zh: 你认为我们在等什么？

sentences.en: A pause?
sentences.zh: 停顿？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: We're waiting for a pause in the conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们在等谈话中的停顿。

sentences.en: Now, why do we need a pause in the conversation before we join?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们在加入之前需要谈话中的停顿？

sentences.en: We don't want to interrupt them basically, right?
sentences.zh: 我们不想打断他们，对吧？

sentences.en: So we want to wait for a little pause.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要等一个小停顿。

sentences.en: We'll move a little bit closer.
sentences.zh: 我们会走近一点。

sentences.en: And then as we join, we make some kind of a comment or ask a question that's on topic.
sentences.zh: 然后加入时，我们会发表评论或提出一个切题的问题。

sentences.en: Now, those are very, very concrete steps for what we call peer entry.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我们所说的“同伴切入”的具体步骤。

sentences.en: But do you think that, you know, a kid with autism could actually pick up on these steps and learn how to actually do that?
sentences.zh: 但你认为自闭症孩子真的能掌握这些步骤并学会如何做到吗？

sentences.en: It seems like it would be challenging for them to learn that.
sentences.zh: 这看起来对他们来说很有挑战性。

sentences.en: It can be challenging, but the great thing is that not only do we rely on these concrete kind of rules and steps of social behavior, which
sentences.zh: 这确实很有挑战性，但好消息是，我们不仅依赖这些具体的社交行为规则和步骤，

sentences.en: is actually, by the way, a really helpful way of teaching kids with autism because they think so concretely and so literally.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这对教导自闭症孩子非常有帮助，因为他们的思维非常具体和刻板。

sentences.en: We're taking something that seems abstract and we're making it very black and white for them.
sentences.zh: 我们把看似抽象的东西变得非黑即白。

sentences.en: But it's not just enough to actually teach them those rules and steps.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅教给他们这些规则和步骤是不够的。

sentences.en: Next, we actually have to demonstrate what that looks like.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们必须演示它看起来是什么样的。

sentences.en: And that's where the role-playing comes in.
sentences.zh: 这就是角色扮演发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: We do a lot of role-playing demonstrations in our groups of sort of the social skills that you want to use, but also the behaviors that you don't want to engage in.
sentences.zh: 我们在小组中进行了大量的角色扮演演示，展示你想要使用的社交技能，以及你不应该参与的行为。

sentences.en: So we show good and bad examples of social behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以我们展示了社交行为的好例子和坏例子。

sentences.en: And then we kind of have them take on the perspectives of the other people and ask them things like, you know, what do you think that was like for that group of people?
sentences.zh: 然后让他们站在其他人的角度思考，问他们：“你觉得那群人当时是什么感觉？”

sentences.en: What do you think they thought of them?
sentences.zh: “你觉得他们是怎么看那个人的？”

sentences.en: I'm going to want to talk to them again.
sentences.zh: “我还会想再和他们说话吗？”

sentences.en: Those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的问题。

sentences.en: And from there, the next step is that there should be some kind of a behavioral rehearsal where they're practicing the newly learned skills.
sentences.zh: 在此之后，下一步应该是某种行为排练，让他们练习新学到的技能。

sentences.en: We're giving them coaching in the moment because, as you say, they don't get it right away.
sentences.zh: 我们会在当下给予指导，因为正如你所说，他们不会马上掌握。

sentences.en: They're not going to master it perfectly.
sentences.zh: 他们不可能完美地掌握它。

sentences.en: And then to generalize these skills to other settings, we need to actually provide some kind of homework assignment where they're practicing the skill in the real world,
sentences.zh: 为了将这些技能推广到其他环境，我们需要提供某种家庭作业，让他们在现实世界中练习这些技能，

sentences.en: essentially.
sentences.zh: 本质上是这样。

sentences.en: What about younger children with autism?
sentences.zh: 那患有自闭症的年幼儿童呢？

sentences.en: I'm sure this is something that concerns parents and teachers, trying to get them to engage more socially.
sentences.zh: 我相信这是家长和老师关心的问题，即如何让他们更多地参与社交。

sentences.en: You know, is there anything that you do differently with younger children?
sentences.zh: 对于年幼的孩子，你们有什么不同的做法吗？

sentences.en: You know, one of the things that's sort of unique about peers is that it's actually a parent-assisted program.
sentences.zh: 你知道，PEERS的一个独特之处在于它是一个家长辅助项目。

sentences.en: You know, the vast majority of social skills programs do not include parents or caregivers in the treatment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，绝大多数社交技能项目在治疗中并不包括家长或看护人。

sentences.en: And I think that's a really big mistake because parents act as social coaches to their kids all the time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个很大的错误，因为家长一直充当着孩子的社交教练。

sentences.en: But as we just discovered in that last example, the advice that they give isn't always the best advice.
sentences.zh: 但正如我们在上一个例子中发现的那样，他们给出的建议并不总是最好的建议。

sentences.en: They might tell their kid to go up and say hello or go up and say hi.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会告诉孩子走过去打个招呼。

sentences.en: So instead, we want to include them on the treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望把他们纳入治疗中。

sentences.en: And so that's what sort of makes our program unique.
sentences.zh: 这就是让我们的项目与众不同的地方。

sentences.en: And in addition to working with adolescents and teens and their parents, we also work with younger kids through our program.
sentences.zh: 除了与青少年及其家长合作外，我们还通过我们的项目与年幼的孩子合作。

sentences.en: We have a program that just was recently developed called Peers for Preschoolers, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们最近开发了一个名为“学龄前儿童PEERS”的项目。

sentences.en: And this program actually works with preschool kids with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
sentences.zh: 这个项目实际上是针对患有自闭症谱系障碍的学龄前儿童的。

sentences.en: And we're teaching social skills using that same method of very concrete rules and steps of social behavior.
sentences.zh: 我们使用同样的方法，即非常具体的社交行为规则和步骤来教授社交技能。

sentences.en: They're much more simplified, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，这些规则要简化得多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I can imagine.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象。

sentences.en: But then also including parents on that and providing role play demonstrations and behavioral
sentences.zh: 但同时也要让家长参与进来，提供角色扮演演示和行为

sentences.en: rehearsal opportunities, lots of homework assignments, and helping parents to learn how to organize things like playdates for their kids.
sentences.zh: 排练机会，布置大量的家庭作业，并帮助家长学习如何为孩子组织游戏约会等活动。

sentences.en: You know, really the crux of all of this really comes down to social interaction and engagement with peers.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这一切的核心归根结底是社交互动和与同伴的接触。

sentences.en: And for younger kids, that really is the responsibility of a parent.
sentences.zh: 对于年幼的孩子，这确实是家长的责任。

sentences.en: For older, you know, adolescents and for adults, that's their responsibility.
sentences.zh: 对于年龄较大的青少年和成年人，那是他们自己的责任。

sentences.en: And they can use support from their parents.
sentences.zh: 他们可以利用家长的支持。

sentences.en: But for our younger kids, they need a lot more support in providing these social opportunities.
sentences.zh: 但对于我们的年幼孩子，他们在提供这些社交机会方面需要更多的支持。

sentences.en: So the parent involvement, I think, is really the key piece to the success of this program.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为家长的参与是这个项目成功的关键。

sentences.en: Is there anything else that you wanted to talk about?
sentences.zh: 还有什么你想谈的吗？

sentences.en: Anything exciting that you're working on with peers?
sentences.zh: 有什么关于PEERS的令人兴奋的事情吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're working on a lot of really exciting things right now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们现在正在做很多非常令人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: So I've talked a lot about the parent assistant portion of this program, that we include parents as social coaches to their kids through peers.
sentences.zh: 我已经谈了很多关于这个项目的家长辅助部分，即我们通过PEERS将家长作为孩子的社交教练。

sentences.en: We've also done some work in the schools where we actually include teachers as the social coaches.
sentences.zh: 我们还在学校做了一些工作，实际上把老师作为社交教练。

sentences.en: And in this case, these programs are teacher facilitated.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，这些项目是由老师引导的。

sentences.en: We teach social skills in the classroom, much like we would teach math or science, something like that, using these very concrete rules and steps.
sentences.zh: 我们在课堂上教授社交技能，就像教数学或科学一样，通过非常具体的规则和步骤来进行教学。

sentences.en: And we have a school-based manual that's actually coming out now that's based on the research that we've done with our peers' school-based prograMs. So we're
sentences.zh: 我们有一本基于学校的指导手册即将出版，它基于我们与同伴学校项目所做的研究。所以我们

sentences.en: very excited about that.
sentences.zh: 对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And that's due out in October 2013.
sentences.zh: 该手册预计于2013年10月出版。

sentences.en: So that's something to look for.
sentences.zh: 所以敬请期待。

sentences.en: And we also have another resource that will be available to families.
sentences.zh: 我们还有另一项资源将提供给各个家庭。

sentences.en: And that's a parent book that's coming out in September of 2013.
sentences.zh: 那是一本将于2013年9月出版的家长手册。

sentences.en: And that's called The Science of Making Friends.
sentences.zh: 书名是《交友的科学》。

sentences.en: And the idea behind this book is that we're actually trying to provide the skills, the rules and steps
sentences.zh: 这本书背后的理念是，我们试图将我们在同伴项目中教授的社交行为技能、规则和步骤，

sentences.en: of social behavior that we teach in peers to families that might not be able to access a peers program in their community or their school.
sentences.zh: 提供给那些在社区或学校无法接触到同伴项目的家庭。

sentences.en: You know, we work really hard on trying to disseminate our program throughout the world, really.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们确实非常努力地尝试在世界各地推广我们的项目。

sentences.en: We do trainings all over the globe.
sentences.zh: 我们在全球各地进行培训。

sentences.en: But the reality is that you can't access a peers program in every community.
sentences.zh: 但现实情况是，并非每个社区都能接触到同伴项目。

sentences.en: And because we know parents are very desperate, very often to help their kids with their social skills, we've provided this parent book,
sentences.zh: 因为我们知道家长们往往非常渴望帮助孩子提升社交技能，所以我们提供了这本家长手册，

sentences.en: The Science of Making Friends.
sentences.zh: 即《交友的科学》。

sentences.en: So we're real excited about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们对此感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Well, it sounds like you have a lot going on.
sentences.zh: 听起来你们有很多工作在进行。

sentences.en: It's very exciting.
sentences.zh: 这非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for joining us today, Dr. Lugson.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您今天加入我们，Lugson博士。

sentences.en: Well, thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 好的，非常感谢你们的邀请。

sentences.en: For more information on the peers program, please visit our website at apa.org slash speakingofpsychology.
sentences.zh: 欲了解更多关于同伴项目的信息，请访问我们的网站 apa.org/speakingofpsychology。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的收听。

sentences.en: I'm Audrey Hamilton with the American
sentences.zh: 我是Audrey Hamilton，来自美国

sentences.en: Psychological Association's Speaking of Psychology.
sentences.zh: 心理学协会的《心理学谈话》节目。
